## The problem

Our twelve-person engineering team still relies on long-lived feature branches, and it's slowing us down. Branches routinely live for two to three weeks before merging, and by the time they land, they've drifted far enough from main that integration becomes a multi-day ordeal. Last month alone, three release candidates slipped because merge conflicts consumed nearly a full sprint. Code review quality suffers too: reviewers face sprawling diffs and rubber-stamp changes they can't reasonably absorb. We are optimizing for isolated progress at the expense of shippable software.

- Merge conflicts and integration pain scale with branch age, not team size, so this problem will only worsen as we grow.
- Large diffs make code review superficial, letting defects slip past reviewers overwhelmed by scope.
- Feature branches hide integration risk until the end of a cycle, when it's most expensive to fix.

## The proposal

I propose we adopt trunk-based development: every engineer commits directly to main at least daily, using feature flags to hide incomplete work. This requires two supporting investments.

- A CI pipeline fast and reliable enough (under ten minutes, no flaky tests) that frequent merges don't become their own bottleneck.
- A lightweight feature-flag system so unfinished work stays invisible to users without needing a separate branch.

Teams that make this switch consistently report shorter cycle times and fewer integration surprises, because small, frequent merges surface conflicts while they're still cheap to resolve, rather than letting them compound for weeks.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is real: trunk-based development demands testing discipline our current suite doesn't fully support, and a broken main blocks everyone, not just one branch's owner. If our CI is flaky, frequent merges could mean frequent, team-wide disruption instead of fewer conflicts — trading one pain for a worse one. This is a legitimate risk, not a reason to dismiss the proposal; it's a reason to treat CI reliability as a prerequisite we fix first, not an afterthought we hope works out. We should also expect a rough adjustment period as people relearn habits around smaller commits and flag hygiene.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
